s: India's National Health Accounts, prepared by NHATS under NHSRC, use which framework?
x: The NHA use the System of Health Accounts 2011 (with NHA Guidelines 2016); the first NHA was for 2013-14.

s: The government share of India's Total Health Expenditure rose from 28.6% in 2013-14 to what level in 2022-23?
x: The government share rose to 43.7%; 39.4% is the OOPE share during COVID-19.

s: During COVID-19, household out-of-pocket expenditure fell to what share of Total Health Expenditure?
x: OOPE fell to 39.4% of THE during COVID-19, when government health expenditure peaked; 28.6% was the government share in 2013–14.

s: Government Health Expenditure reached what percentage of GDP during the COVID peak in 2021–22?
x: GHE reached 1.84% of GDP during the COVID peak in 2021–22.

s: According to the Economic Survey 2021-22, what percentage of GDP did the Centre and States together spend on health in 2019-20?
x: Centre and States together spent about 1.3% of GDP on health in 2019–20.

s: For which year were the first National Health Accounts estimates in India prepared?
x: India's first NHA was for 2013-14.

s: According to NHA 2022-23, what was the share of social security expenditure in Total Health Expenditure?
x: Social security's share rose from 6% (2013-14) to 9.9% (2022-23).

s: According to National Health Accounts 2022-23, what was Government Health Expenditure as a share of GDP?
x: NHA 2022-23 puts GHE at 1.43% of GDP, up from 1.15% in 2013-14 but below the 2.5% NHP 2017 target.

s: Which of the following statements regarding the National Health Policy, 2017 target is correct?
o: It targeted GHE of 2.5% of GDP by 2022, with the Centre contributing 60%.
It targeted GHE of 1.5% of GDP by 2025, with the States contributing 40%.
It targeted GHE of 2.5% of GDP by 2025, with the Centre contributing 40% of public spending.
It targeted GHE of 3% of GDP by 2030, with no specified Centre share.
x: NHP 2017 targeted Government Health Expenditure of 2.5% of GDP by 2025, with the Centre’s share intended to be 40% of public spending. The target was missed.

s: Which of the following pairs relating to the 15th Finance Commission health grants is correctly matched?
o: Coverage – only urban health and wellness centres
x: The 15th FC recommended ₹70,051 crore for 2021–26 through local governments, covering rural and building-less SCs/PHCs/CHCs too, not only urban HWCs.

s: The 15th Finance Commission recommended health grants of approximately what amount through local governments for the period 2021–2026?
x: The 15th Finance Commission recommended health grants amounting to ₹70,051 crore through local governments for 2021–2026.

s: Under the National Health Policy 2017, what was to be the Centre's share of public health spending?
x: NHP 2017 set the Centre's share at 40% of public health spending, along with GHE of 2.5% of GDP by 2025.

s: Which of the following correctly represents the trend in OOPE as a share of Total Health Expenditure between 2013–14 and 2022–23?
x: OOPE declined from 64.2% of Total Health Expenditure in 2013–14 to 43.4% in 2022–23, although it remained about half of current health expenditure.

s: Which of the following components account for over 50% of OOPE because they are generally not covered by insurance?
o: Only inpatient surgery and intensive care
Ambulance services and health education alone
x: Outpatient care, diagnostics and medicines account for over half of OOPE because insurance commonly does not cover them.

s: What does the term 'missing middle' refer to in health financing?
o: More than 40 crore Indians lacking financial protection
People covered simultaneously by both public and private insurance
The middle-income group receiving free medicines at public facilities
Households whose insurance claims are pending for less than one month
x: The “missing middle” refers to more than 40 crore Indians who lack adequate financial protection; NITI Aayog first flagged the term.

s: Which body flagged the term 'missing middle' for Indians without financial protection for health?
x: NITI Aayog flagged the 'missing middle' of over 40 crore Indians without health cover.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA)?
o: It fixes ceiling prices of scheduled drugs
Scheduled drugs are those in the National List of Essential Medicines
Its price control operates under the Drugs Price Control Order, 2013
x: NPPA was established in 1997; 2013 is the year of the Drugs Price Control Order under which it fixes ceiling prices.

s: In which year was the Clinical Establishments Act, adopted by only about 11 States and 6 UTs, enacted?
x: The Act dates to 2010; 2013 is the Drugs Price Control Order and 2017 the National Health Policy.

s: DVDMS is associated with which function in the public medicine-supply system?
o: Setting the list of essential surgical procedures
x: DVDMS manages drug procurement and inventory under the Free Drugs Service Initiative.

s: How many Jan Aushadhi Kendras had been opened by December 2025?
x: 17,990 Jan Aushadhi Kendras had opened by Dec 2025; 25,000 is the target for March 2027.

s: In which year was the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) set up?
x: NPPA was set up in 1997; it fixes ceiling prices under the Drugs Price Control Order 2013.

s: Which body fixes the ceiling prices of drugs in the National List of Essential Medicines (NLEM)?
x: The NPPA (1997) fixes ceiling prices of scheduled NLEM drugs under the Drugs Price Control Order, 2013.

s: What is the target number of Jan Aushadhi Kendras to be opened by March 2027?
x: 17,990 Kendras had opened by December 2025, with a target of 25,000 by March 2027.

s: PM-JAY provides health cover of how much per family per year?
x: PM-JAY covers ₹5 lakh per family per year; ₹25 lakh is AP's Universal Health Policy cover.

s: On what basis was PM-JAY extended to all citizens aged 70 and above in October 2024?
o: Only if not covered by any other scheme
x: The October 2024 extension covers all citizens aged 70+, irrespective of income, through the Ayushman Vay Vandana card.

s:
Consider the following statements about the 2024 PM-JAY extension for senior citizens:
1. Beneficiaries receive the Ayushman Vay Vandana card.
2. Members aged 70+ of already covered families get an extra ₹5 lakh top-up.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: the 70+ cover uses the Ayushman Vay Vandana card and gives a ₹5 lakh top-up to already covered families.

s: On the basis of which data are PM-JAY beneficiary families identified?
x: PM-JAY identifies poor and vulnerable families from SECC 2011 deprivation data.

s: Which is the world's largest health assurance scheme?
x: PM-JAY, launched on 23 September 2018, is described by the Government as the largest health assurance scheme in the world.

s: About how many families does Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY aim to cover?
x: PM-JAY aims to cover over 12 crore families, nearly 55 crore people, with ₹5 lakh per family per year.

s: What is the Centre–State sharing ratio of PM-JAY funds for most States?
x: The Centre and most States share PM-JAY costs 60:40; North-Eastern and three Himalayan States/UTs share 90:10.

s:
Consider the following statements about the funding of PM-JAY:
1. The Centre and the North-Eastern States share the cost in the ratio 90:10.
2. For Union Territories without a legislature, the Centre can bear up to 100% of the cost.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: North-Eastern and three Himalayan States/UTs share 90:10, and the Centre can fund up to 100% for UTs without a legislature.

s: Which of the following is regarded as a criticism of insurance-led health financing models?
o: They provide universal outpatient coverage in all circumstances.
They increase coverage without necessarily increasing the availability of care.
They reduce coverage while automatically increasing the quality of care.
They eliminate the need for primary healthcare expenditure.
x: A stated criticism is that insurance-led models may expand coverage without a corresponding increase in actual care. Greater spending on primary care and outpatient care is suggested as part of the corrective approach.

s: By about how much did government-financed health insurance coverage in India rise between 2017-18 and 2025?
x: NSS 80th round shows government-financed insurance up 2.5-fold.

s: According to NFHS-6, households with at least one insured member rose from 41.0% to what level?
x: NFHS-6 shows insured households rising from 41.0% to 60.2%.

s: In which year and city did the Central Government Health Scheme (CGHS) begin?
x: CGHS was started in 1954 in Delhi for Central Government employees and pensioners.

s: Where was the Employees' State Insurance (ESI) Scheme inaugurated in 1952?
x: The ESI Scheme was inaugurated at Kanpur on 24 February 1952 by Prime Minister Nehru, now ESIC Day.

s: In which year was the Employees' State Insurance Act passed?
x: The ESI Act was passed in 1948; the scheme itself started in 1952.

s: Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva, formerly known as YSR Aarogyasri, is primarily intended to provide which of the following?
o: Subsidised insurance exclusively for private-sector employees
Free crop insurance to small farmers
Pension support to retired government employees
Cashless health assurance to economically vulnerable families in Andhra Pradesh
x: Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva, earlier YSR Aarogyasri, is Andhra Pradesh’s flagship cashless health assurance scheme for economically vulnerable families.

s: Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva in Andhra Pradesh is implemented in convergence with which scheme, enabling portability and wider empanelment?
x: The AP scheme runs in convergence with PM-JAY, providing portability and wider hospital empanelment.

s: Andhra Pradesh's Universal Health Policy (Sep 2025) provides cover of up to how much per family per year?
x: The policy offers up to ₹25 lakh per family per year covering all 3,257 procedures.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Andhra Pradesh's Universal Health Policy (2025)?
o: Claims up to ₹2.5 lakh are handled through insurers
Employees under the Employee Health Scheme are included
Claims from ₹2.5 lakh to ₹25 lakh go through the NTR Vaidya Seva Trust
x: EHS employees are excluded from the Universal Health Policy; the other statements are correct.

s: Together with EHS, RSBY, ESIS and CGHS, AP's state health scheme covers about what share of AP households (2026)?
x: The state scheme with EHS, RSBY, ESIS and CGHS covers about 70% of AP households.

s: How much did the Andhra Pradesh Budget 2024-25 allocate to the NTR Vaidya Seva Trust?
x: AP Budget 2024-25 gave ₹18,732 crore to health, including ₹4,000 crore to the NTR Vaidya Seva Trust.

s: Who are covered by Andhra Pradesh's Employee Health Scheme (EHS)?
o: Families below the poverty line only
State Government employees, pensioners and their dependants
Workers in the organised private sector
x: EHS gives cashless treatment to AP State Government employees, pensioners and their dependants; CGHS covers Central employees.

s: In which years were the National Rural Health Mission (NRHM) and the National Urban Health Mission (NUHM) launched respectively?
x: NRHM was launched in 2005 and NUHM in 2013; together they form the National Health Mission.

s: Which scheme entitles pregnant women to free ('zero expense') delivery and newborn care at public facilities?
x: JSSK is the free-entitlement scheme; JSY gives cash assistance for institutional delivery and is 100% centrally sponsored.

s: What is the usual Centre–State funding pattern under the National Health Mission?
o: 60:40, with 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States
x: The normal funding pattern is 60:40 between the Centre and States, while North-Eastern and Himalayan States receive a 90:10 pattern.

s: Which age group of adolescents does the Rashtriya Kishor Swasthya Karyakram (RKSK) cover?
x: RKSK covers 10-19 year-olds through Adolescent Friendly Health Clinics, weekly iron folic acid supplementation and peer educators.

s: Which of the following pairs relating to ASHA is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Level of work – Block-level medical officer
Role – Link between households and the health system
Level of work – Village-level community health worker
x: ASHA is a village-level community health worker who, with the ANM, links rural households to the health system; she is not a block-level medical officer.

s: In which year was Anaemia Mukt Bharat launched?
x: Anaemia Mukt Bharat was launched in 2018 and follows the 6x6x6 strategy; 2014 is wrong.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Mobile Academy – Weekly audio messages to mothers
x: JSY gives cash for institutional delivery. JSSK gives free delivery, RKSK covers adolescents of 10–19 years, and Mobile Academy is an audio course for ASHAs (Kilkari sends messages to mothers).

s: Which National Health Mission scheme gives cash assistance for institutional delivery?
x: Janani Suraksha Yojana gives cash for institutional delivery and is 100% centrally sponsored; JSSK gives free, zero-expense delivery.

s: What is the Centre–State funding ratio under the National Health Mission for North-Eastern and Himalayan States?
x: NHM funding is usually 60:40, but 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States.

s: What does the Kilkari service under the National Health Mission provide?
o: 72 free weekly audio messages from the second trimester till the child turns one
An audio training course for ASHAs
x: Kilkari sends 72 free weekly audio messages to families; Mobile Academy is the audio course for ASHAs.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY):
1. It gives cash assistance for institutional delivery.
2. It is 100% centrally sponsored.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: JSY gives cash for institutional delivery and is fully centrally sponsored; JSSK gives free delivery.

s: How many ASHAs does Andhra Pradesh have (2026)?
x: AP has 42,060 ASHAs; 10,032 is the number of Village Health Clinics.

s: What is Mobile Academy under the National Health Mission?
o: Weekly audio messages to pregnant women
An audio training course for ASHAs
x: Mobile Academy is an audio course for ASHAs; Kilkari sends weekly audio messages to families.

s: When was the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission launched?
x: ABDM was launched in September 2021; PM-ABHIM followed on 25 October 2021.

s: ABHA, the health ID under the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission, has how many digits?
x: ABHA is a 14-digit health ID; accounts crossed 90 crore by June 2026.

s: Which body implements the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission?
x: ABDM, launched in September 2021, is implemented by the National Health Authority, not NITI Aayog.

s: For whom did the National Medical Commission's March 2026 direction require medical colleges to generate and link ABHA IDs?
o: All OPD, IPD and emergency patients
x: The NMC directed medical colleges to generate and link ABHA IDs for all OPD, IPD and emergency patients, partly to detect fake patients during inspections.

s: What is eSanjeevani, now equipped with a Clinical Decision Support System?
x: eSanjeevani is a telemedicine service, now with a Clinical Decision Support System.

s: To which scheme does Arogya Mitra, often confused with ABDM components, actually belong?
x: Arogya Mitra is the PM-JAY hospital facilitator, not a component of ABDM.

s: Which ABDM component is meant for testing?
x: The Sandbox is ABDM's testing component; UHI and the Consent Manager are gateways and the Drug Registry is a registry.

s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four principal registries of ABDM?
x: The four registries are ABHA, Healthcare Professionals Registry, Health Facility Registry and Drug Registry. Arogya Mitra is not an ABDM component.

s: Which was the first State to link the electronic health records of one crore people to the ABDM database?
x: Andhra Pradesh was the first State to link the health records of one crore people to the ABDM database.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission:
1. Andhra Pradesh was the first State to link the electronic health records of one crore people to it.
2. It is implemented by NITI Aayog.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: AP was first to link one crore records; ABDM is implemented by the National Health Authority, not NITI Aayog.

s: What kind of digital health ecosystem does the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission aim to build?
o: A closed one run only by private hospitals
x: ABDM aims at a consent-based, interoperable digital health ecosystem so patient records can be shared across providers.

s: Which of the following is a gateway of the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission?
x: ABDM's gateways are the Health Information Consent Manager, UHI and NHCX; Arogya Mitra belongs to PM-JAY.

s: By June 2026, how many ABHA accounts had been created?
x: Over 90 crore ABHA (14-digit health ID) accounts had been created by June 2026.

s: Mission Indradhanush aims at what level of full immunisation?
x: The December 2014 catch-up drive under UIP for zero-dose and partly immunised children targets 90% full immunisation.

s: Which one of the following sets of vaccines is administered at birth under the Universal Immunisation Programme?
o: BCG, OPV-0 and Hepatitis B birth dose
MR-2, DPT booster-1 and OPV booster
Td, DPT booster-2 and Rotavirus vaccine
x: The birth schedule includes BCG, OPV-0 and the birth dose of Hepatitis B.

s: Under the Universal Immunisation Programme schedule, which one of the following vaccine-age pairs is correctly matched?
x: MR-1 is given at 9-12 months (the correct PYQ pair). Td is given at 10 and 16 years, not 5-6 years; OPV-1 is given at 6 weeks, not 16-24 months (when the OPV booster is given); DPT booster-2 is given at 5-6 years, not 6 weeks.

s: Under the Universal Immunisation Programme, at what ages are the primary doses of pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV) given?
x: PCV is given at 6 and 14 weeks, with a booster at 9-12 months.

s: Under the UIP schedule, at what age is Td (tetanus and adult diphtheria) given?
x: Td is given at 10 and 16 years; at 5–6 years it is DPT booster-2, a common trap.

s: What is U-WIN a digital registry for?
o: Routine immunisation of pregnant women and children
x: U-WIN is the digital registry of routine immunisation for pregnant women and children.

s: Whom does Mission Indradhanush, launched in December 2014, mainly reach?
x: Mission Indradhanush is a catch-up drive under UIP for zero-dose and partly immunised children, targeting 90% full immunisation.

s: Under the Universal Immunisation Programme, at what age is the DPT booster-2 given?
x: DPT booster-2 is given at 5–6 years; DPT booster-1 is at 16–24 months and Td at 10 and 16 years.

s: Under the Universal Immunisation Programme, at what ages are pentavalent and rotavirus vaccines given?
x: Pentavalent, rotavirus and OPV 1–3 are given at 6, 10 and 14 weeks.

s: Which pillar of Ayushman Bharat provides comprehensive primary care?
x: Ayushman Arogya Mandirs provide comprehensive primary care. PM-JAY is the hospitalisation assurance pillar, ABDM the digital backbone and PM-ABHIM the health infrastructure pillar.

s: Primary care, delivered through Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, is expected to meet about what share of health needs?
x: Primary care meets 80-90% of health needs; the AAM target was 1,50,000 centres and over 1.73 lakh have been converted.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about PM-ABHIM?
o: It focuses on health infrastructure for pandemics
Its approved outlay of ₹64,180 crore covers FY 2016–17 to FY 2020–21
It was launched on 25 October 2021 at Varanasi
It includes critical care blocks, Integrated Public Health Laboratories and BSL-3 laboratories
x: The ₹64,180 crore outlay covers FY 2021–22 to FY 2025–26.

s: Where was PM-ABHIM launched on 25 October 2021?
x: The Prime Minister launched PM-ABHIM at Varanasi on 25 October 2021.

s: What is the outlay of PM-ABHIM (2021-22 to 2025-26)?
x: PM-ABHIM has an outlay of ₹64,180 crore, the largest pan-India health infrastructure scheme.

s: What was the target number of Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (earlier AB-HWCs)?
x: The target was 1,50,000; over 1.73 lakh have been converted.

s: Which scheme is described as the largest pan-India scheme for health infrastructure?
x: PM-ABHIM, with an outlay of ₹64,180 crore (2021-26), is the largest pan-India health infrastructure scheme.

s: From where were the Critical Care Blocks and IPHLs under PM-ABHIM in Andhra Pradesh inaugurated in September 2026?
x: J.P. Nadda inaugurated 10 Critical Care Blocks and 12 IPHLs (₹250 crore) from Vijayawada.

s: World Health Day is observed on 7 April because of which event of 1948?
o: the World Health Organization was founded, with its headquarters at Geneva
the Alma-Ata Declaration on primary health care was adopted
the World Health Organization was founded, with its headquarters at New York
smallpox was declared eradicated by the World Health Assembly
x: WHO was founded on 7 April 1948 and is headquartered at Geneva, so World Health Day falls on 7 April. WHO's headquarters is not New York; the Alma-Ata Declaration and the eradication of smallpox are later events and not linked to 7 April 1948.

s:
Consider the following statements about the World Health Organization:
1. Its headquarters is at Geneva.
2. Its membership reached 194 in 2013.
3. The second term of its Director-General ends in 2025.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: WHO is at Geneva and has had 194 members since 2013. Tedros's second term ends on 15 August 2027, not 2025.

s: What is the theme of World Health Day 2026?
o: Together for health. Stand with science
x: World Health Day 2026 theme is 'Together for health. Stand with science'.

s: Who is the Director-General of the World Health Organization?
x: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus heads WHO; his second term ends on 15 August 2027.

s: When does the second term of WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus end?
x: Tedros's second term ends on 15 August 2027; 7 candidates were nominated to succeed him.

s: In which year was the Indian Research Fund Association, the predecessor of ICMR, established?
x: The Indian Research Fund Association was established in 1911 and was later renamed the ICMR in 1949.

s: Which of the following is an ICMR-related initiative?
x: The India TB Research Consortium is listed among ICMR initiatives, with MERA India and the India Hypertension Control Initiative. India Food Security Consortium is not an ICMR initiative; Eat Right India is FSSAI's and U-WIN is the immunisation registry.

s: How many pillars does ICMR's Strategic Plan 2017-24 ('Vision 2030') have?
x: Vision 2030 has 5 pillars and 15 goals.

s: Which of the following is NOT a pillar of ICMR's 'Vision 2030' strategic plan?
x: The five pillars are capacity building, data management, leveraging traditional medicine, evidence to policy, and strengthening programme implementation through research; health insurance is not one.

s: In which year was the Indian Research Fund Association renamed ICMR?
x: IRFA, set up in 1911, was renamed ICMR in 1949.

s: Which of the following is an ICMR initiative?
x: The India Hypertension Control Initiative is an ICMR initiative; Eat Right India is FSSAI's and Kilkari is under NHM.

s: In which year was India's first National Health Policy issued?
x: India's National Health Policies came in 1983, 2002 and 2017.

s: In which year was Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY launched?
x: PM-JAY was launched in September 2018, after the AB-HWCs in April 2018.

s: In which year was the National Policy for Rare Diseases issued?
x: The National Policy for Rare Diseases came in 2021, the same year as ABDM and PM-ABHIM.

s: Which approach does the National Health Policy, 2017 follow?
o: A private-sector-only approach to emergency care
An assurance-based approach with comprehensive primary care
An insurance-only approach without public-sector services
A disease-specific approach limited to communicable diseases
x: NHP 2017 adopted an assurance-based approach and envisaged comprehensive primary care rather than an insurance-only or disease-specific model.

s: Along with increased public spending on health, what did the National Health Policy, 2002 emphasise?
o: Withdrawal of the Centre from health funding
Exclusive provision of health services by the public sector
A larger role for the private sector and NGOs
x: NHP 2002 called for more public spending and a larger role for the private sector and NGOs, not exclusive public provision.

s: The National Health Policy, 2017 set a life expectancy target of how many years by 2025?
x: NHP 2017 aimed to raise life expectancy from 67.5 to 70 years by 2025, alongside 2.5% of GDP public spending and TFR 2.1.

s: Under the National Health Policy, 2017, public health spending was targeted at what share of GDP by 2025?
x: NHP 2017 targeted public health spending of 2.5% of GDP by 2025; it was missed, at 1.43% in 2022-23.

s:
Consider the following statements about the National Health Policy, 2017 targets:
1. Total fertility rate of 2.1 by 2025.
2. Public health spending of 1.43% of GDP by 2025.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: NHP 2017 set a TFR of 2.1 by 2025. Its spending target was 2.5% of GDP; 1.43% is the level actually reached in 2022-23.

s: Who launched the Eat Right India campaign (2018)?
x: Eat Right India is an FSSAI campaign; FSSAI was created under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

s: The Eat Right India and Fit India campaigns together seek to reduce deaths due to which diseases?
x: Together, Eat Right India and Fit India aim to reduce deaths caused by non-communicable diseases through healthier diets and increased physical activity.

s: In which year was the Fit India Movement launched?
x: Fit India Movement began in 2019 to bring fitness into daily life; Swachh Bharat was 2014 and Eat Right India 2018.

s: Under which Act was FSSAI, which runs Eat Right India, created?
x: FSSAI was created under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

s: What is the main public health objective of the Swachh Bharat Abhiyan (2014)?
o: Sanitation and hygiene for disease prevention
x: Swachh Bharat aims at sanitation and hygiene to prevent disease; Fit India is about fitness and Eat Right India about diets.

s: With which of the following is Andhra Pradesh's Sanjeevani digital health programme (from August 2026) mainly associated?
o: Replacement of all public hospitals by private hospitals
Universal distribution of fortified food through fair-price shops
Free insurance cover of ₹5 lakh for every citizen
A digital health profile and ABHA ID for every citizen
x: Sanjeevani aims to create a digital health profile and ABHA ID for every citizen of Andhra Pradesh.

s: Where are telemedicine services available in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Only private hospitals empanelled under PM-JAY
None of the Ayushman Arogya Mandirs
x: Telemedicine is available in all Ayushman Arogya Mandirs in Andhra Pradesh (APPSC 2024); it is not confined to AIIMS Mangalagiri or empanelled private hospitals.

s: Where was Andhra Pradesh's Family Physician programme launched on 6 April 2023?
x: The Family Doctor programme was launched on 6 April 2023 at Lingamguntla, Chilakaluripet mandal (Palnadu).

s: Under AP's Family Physician programme, doctors give preventive care through about how many YSR Village Health Clinics?
x: Doctors work through 10,032 YSR Village Health Clinics; 42,060 is the number of ASHAs in AP.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: RTS,S/AS01 (Mosquirix) was the first WHO-approved malaria vaccine.
BCG is a vaccine for tuberculosis.
A licensed vaccine against HIV/AIDS is in routine use.
R21/Matrix-M was developed through collaboration between the Oxford Jenner Institute and Serum Institute.
x: Option C is incorrect: no licensed vaccine against HIV/AIDS exists yet. Mosquirix was the first WHO-approved malaria vaccine, BCG prevents TB and R21 came from Oxford and Serum Institute.

s: NACP Phase V (2021-26) aims at what cut in new HIV infections and AIDS deaths?
x: NACP Phase V (2021-26) aims at an 80% cut in new infections and AIDS deaths, not 50%.

s: What is the full form of VCTC in HIV services?
x: VCTC is the Voluntary Counselling and Testing Centre; ART is free for life at ART centres, and ICTC testing is voluntary with counselling.

s: The HIV and AIDS (Prevention and Control) Act, 2017 primarily seeks to prevent which of the following?
o: Discrimination against people living with HIV
x: The Act of 2017 bars discrimination against people living with HIV and provides a legal framework for their protection.

s: To which organisation does AVAHAN, an HIV prevention initiative in India, belong?
x: AVAHAN is the Gates Foundation's HIV prevention initiative, not a World Bank project; the Red Ribbon Express is an awareness train.

s: What does the third '95' of the UNAIDS 95-95-95 target refer to?
o: People living with HIV knowing their status
Those who know their status being on treatment
Suppressed viral load among those on treatment
x: The three 95s are: know status, be on treatment, and have a suppressed viral load; the third is viral suppression among those on treatment.

s: Which of the following groups of States carries the highest HIV burden in India?
x: Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka are identified as carrying the highest HIV burden among the listed States.

s: What is the full form of ICTC in HIV services?
x: ICTC is the Integrated Counselling and Testing Centre, offering free, voluntary testing with counselling.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Red Ribbon Express – HIV/AIDS awareness train
x: The Red Ribbon Express is an awareness train. AVAHAN is a Gates Foundation prevention initiative, ELISA is a screening test (no HIV vaccine is licensed) and Zidovudine is an anti-retroviral drug.

s: In which year was the National AIDS Control Programme launched?
x: NACP was launched in 1992 and is led by NACO under MoHFW; 1981 is when HIV was first recognised.

s: Which region of the world has the most HIV/AIDS cases?
x: Sub-Saharan Africa has about two-thirds of all HIV/AIDS cases.

s: What does the ELISA test detect in HIV screening?
x: ELISA, the first widely used HIV screening test, detects antibodies.

s: In which year was HIV first recognised?
x: HIV was first recognised in 1981; India's NACP began later, in 1992.

s: In which year was UNAIDS set up?
x: UNAIDS, the joint UN programme on HIV/AIDS, was set up in 1996.

s: Where was the 26th International AIDS Conference, at which the UNAIDS report 'United to end AIDS' (2026) was released, held?
x: The 2026 UNAIDS report 'United to end AIDS' came out at the 26th International AIDS Conference in Rio; it put new infections at a 30-year low.

s:
Match the following phases of the National AIDS Control Programme with their periods:
List-I (Phase)
A. NACP-I
B. NACP-III
C. NACP-IV
D. NACP-V
List-II (Period)
1. 2021–26
2. 1992–99
3. 2012–17
4. 2007–12
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: NACP-I ran 1992–99, NACP-III 2007–12, NACP-IV 2012–17 (extended to 2021) and NACP-V 2021–26.

s: On which date is World AIDS Day observed?
x: World AIDS Day is on 1 December; 24 March is World TB Day and 21 September is World Alzheimer's Day.

s: In which year was the Pulse Polio programme launched?
x: Pulse Polio began in 1995, after India became smallpox-free in 1977; the last wild polio case was in 2011.

s: When did India switch from trivalent to bivalent oral polio vaccine?
x: The switch from tOPV to bOPV took place in April 2016, not 2014; March 2014 is when SEAR was certified polio-free.

s: Who developed the first polio vaccine?
x: Jonas Salk made the first (injected, inactivated) polio vaccine in 1955. Albert Sabin made the oral polio vaccine.

s: Bivalent OPV covers which polio virus types?
x: Bivalent OPV covers types 1 and 3, while trivalent OPV covers types 1, 2 and 3.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: India became smallpox-free in 1977; 2014 is the polio-free certification year.

s: From where was India's last wild polio case reported in January 2011?
x: The last wild polio case was from Howrah, West Bengal, in January 2011.

s: In which year was India declared smallpox-free?
x: India became smallpox-free in 1977; polio certification came in 2014 – do not swap the years.

s: When was the WHO South-East Asia Region, including India, certified polio-free?
x: WHO certified the South-East Asia Region (11 countries including India) polio-free on 27 March 2014.

s: Who developed the oral polio vaccine?
x: Albert Sabin developed the oral polio vaccine; Jonas Salk developed the first, injected polio vaccine.

s: What is the national target year for tuberculosis elimination in India?
x: India’s national target for TB elimination is 2025, five years ahead of the SDG target of 2030.

s: What is Ni-kshay?
o: An insurance scheme for TB patients
A digital portal for TB notification and tracking
x: Ni-kshay is the digital TB notification and tracking portal; Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana gives nutritional DBT to all notified TB patients.

s: By how much did TB mortality in India fall during 2015–2024?
x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (25%); it is added as option 5.
TB mortality fell from 28 to 21 per lakh between 2015 and 2024, a 25% decline; 28% is the 2015 rate mistaken for the fall, and 21% is the fall in incidence.

s: What does the Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana provide?
o: Nutritional DBT to notified TB patients
Adoption of TB patients by Ni-kshay Mitras
x: Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana gives nutritional DBT to all notified TB patients, public and private.

s: Under the PM TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (September 2022), who adopt TB patients?
x: Under PM TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan, Ni-kshay Mitras adopt TB patients.

s: During 2015–2024, to what level did TB treatment coverage in India rise from 53%?
x: Treatment coverage rose from 53% to 92%; treatment success reached 90% in 2025.

s: On which date is World TB Day observed?
x: World TB Day is 24 March; World Alzheimer's Day is 21 September and World AIDS Day 1 December.

s: According to the India TB Report 2024, how many TB cases were notified in India in 2023?
x: India TB Report 2024 recorded 25.52 lakh notifications in 2023, up from 24.22 lakh in 2022.

s: By how much did TB incidence in India fall during 2015–2024?
x: TB incidence fell by 21% between 2015 and 2024, while TB mortality fell by 28%.

s: What was India's TB treatment success rate in 2025?
x: TB treatment success rose from 83% in 2021 to 90% in 2025.

s: Under the TB campaign running since December 2024, how many people had been screened by August 2026?
x: By August 2026 the campaign had screened over 20 crore people and diagnosed over 28 lakh.

s: Andhra Pradesh notified over how many TB cases in 2024?
x: AP notified over 78,000 TB cases in 2024.

s: The National Framework for Malaria Elimination covers which period?
x: The National Framework for Malaria Elimination covers 2016–2030 and targets malaria elimination by 2030.

s: Which of the following is NOT a tool under the National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme for malaria control?
x: IRS, LLINs, larvivorous fish, bio-larvicides and source reduction are listed malaria-control tools. Universal antibiotic prophylaxis is not one of them.

s: Which of the following groups consists only of countries certified malaria-free by WHO?
x: Sri Lanka, China and Timor-Leste are the three countries identified as WHO-certified malaria-free in this group.

s: Who developed RTS,S/AS01 (Mosquirix), the first WHO-approved malaria vaccine?
x: Mosquirix is by GSK; R21/Matrix-M is by Oxford's Jenner Institute with the Serum Institute.

s: Which body leads MERA India, the Malaria Elimination Research Alliance India?
x: MERA India is led by ICMR.

s: Who developed the R21/Matrix-M malaria vaccine?
o: Oxford Jenner Institute and Serum Institute of India
x: R21/Matrix-M was developed by Oxford's Jenner Institute with the Serum Institute of India.

s: Outbreaks of which of the following diseases are handled by the National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme (NVBDCP)?
x: NVBDCP deals with vector-borne diseases such as malaria, dengue and chikungunya.

s: Which was the first country in the WHO South-East Asia Region to be certified malaria-free?
x: The Maldives was first; Sri Lanka (5 September 2016) was the second in the region.

s: Quinine, a medicine for malaria, is obtained from the bark of which tree?
x: Quinine comes from the bark of the Cinchona tree.

s: By how much did malaria cases in India fall between 2015 and 2023?
x: Under the National Framework for Malaria Elimination, malaria cases fell by about 80% during 2015–2023.

s: What is Cervavac, announced in September 2022?
o: India's first indigenous quadrivalent HPV vaccine against cervical cancer, made by the Serum Institute of India
India's first indigenous malaria vaccine, made by Bharat Biotech
An intranasal COVID-19 vaccine developed with ICMR-NIV
The world's first DNA vaccine approved for humans, made by Zydus
x: Cervavac is India's first indigenous quadrivalent HPV vaccine, made by the Serum Institute of India against cervical cancer (Sept 2022). The intranasal COVID vaccine is iNCOVACC; the first DNA vaccine is ZyCoV-D by Zydus; and Cervavac is not a malaria vaccine (R21 is the Oxford-SII malaria vaccine).

s: Diphtheria is prevented by which type of vaccine?
x: Diphtheria is prevented by a toxoid vaccine; hepatitis B also has a vaccine.

s: Shanvac-B, India's first genetically engineered vaccine, protects against which disease?
x: Shanvac-B is a Hepatitis B vaccine and was India's first genetically engineered vaccine.

s: Which of the following is a DNA-based COVID-19 vaccine developed in India?
x: ZyCoV-D is a DNA-based COVID-19 vaccine; Covaxin is an inactivated-virus vaccine.

s: Who developed the HPV vaccine Cervavac, which targets cervical cancer?
x: Cervavac is India's first indigenous quadrivalent HPV vaccine, made by the Serum Institute for cervical cancer.

s: The triple-drug IDA regimen for lymphatic filariasis uses Ivermectin, DEC and which other drug?
x: IDA = Ivermectin, DEC and Albendazole; India targets LF elimination by 2027, three years ahead of the SDG target.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: NP-NCD — Identification of high-risk persons and linkage to care
IDSP — Elimination of premature non-communicable disease deaths by one-third by 2030
IHCI — Reduction of hypertension-related heart attack, stroke and kidney-failure deaths
x: IDSP is concerned with outbreak surveillance. The target of reducing premature NCD deaths by one-third by 2030 belongs to SDG 3.4.

s: Under which programme is free multidrug therapy (MDT) for leprosy provided at PHCs?
x: Free MDT for leprosy at PHCs is under the National Leprosy Eradication Programme (with the Sparsh campaign), not NVBDCP.

s: What is the target year for eliminating measles-rubella in India?
x: Measles-rubella elimination is targeted for 2026; lymphatic filariasis is 2027 and malaria 2030.

s: What is India's target year for eliminating lymphatic filariasis?
x: Lymphatic filariasis elimination is targeted for 2027, three years ahead of the SDG.

s: In which year was the kala-azar elimination target of less than one case per 10,000 in every block achieved?
x: The kala-azar target was achieved in 2023; WHO certification is pending.

s:
Match the following elimination targets of India:
List-I (Disease)
A. Lymphatic filariasis
B. Measles-rubella
C. Malaria
D. Sickle cell anaemia
List-II (Target year)
1. 2026
2. 2027
3. 2030
4. 2047
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Targets: lymphatic filariasis 2027, measles-rubella 2026, malaria 2030 and sickle cell anaemia 2047.

s: In which year was the Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme (IDSP) launched?
x: IDSP was launched in 2004 under NHM for outbreak surveillance.

s: On which date is Anti-Leprosy Day observed in India?
x: Anti-Leprosy Day is 30 January (Gandhi's death anniversary); World Leprosy Day is the last Sunday of January.

s: Where was the National Sickle Cell Anaemia Elimination Mission launched on 1 July 2023?
x: It was launched on 1 July 2023 at Shahdol, Madhya Pradesh, with a tribal focus.

s:
Assertion (A): In sickle cell anaemia, red blood cells cannot carry oxygen properly.
Reason (R): In sickle cell anaemia, the red blood cells become misshapen.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Sickle cell anaemia is inherited; the misshapen red cells cannot carry oxygen properly, so R explains A.

s: How many at-risk people are to be screened under the National Sickle Cell Anaemia Elimination Mission?
x: The mission, launched at Shahdol in 2023, aims to screen 7 crore (70 million) at-risk people.

s: With which disease is the Sparsh awareness campaign associated?
x: Sparsh is the leprosy awareness campaign under NLEP.

s: In which year was Tele-MANAS, the tele-mental health service, launched?
x: Tele-MANAS came in 2022, after the NMHP (1982), the Mental Health Act (1987) and the Mental Healthcare Act (2017).

s: What is the reported mental-health treatment gap in India?
x: The treatment gap is 84.5%, with about one in seven Indians affected and 0.3 psychiatrists per lakh population.

s: In which year was India's first mental health programme, the NMHP, launched?
x: NMHP began in 1982; the Mental Health Act came in 1987 and Tele-MANAS in 2022.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017:
1. It decriminalised suicide.
2. It repealed the Mental Health Act, 1987.
3. It restricted electroconvulsive therapy (ECT).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The 2017 Act decriminalised suicide, restricted ECT, gave a right to access government care and repealed the 1987 Act.

s: Which of the following pairs relating to the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Access to care – Right to access mental healthcare from government services
x: The 2017 Act restricted ECT rather than removing restrictions on it.

s: About how many Indians are affected by mental disorders, as per the burden estimate?
x: About 1 in 7 Indians has a mental disorder; the treatment gap is 84.5%.

s: The India Hypertension Control Initiative, implemented with ICMR, seeks to reduce deaths due to which conditions?
o: Heart attack, stroke and kidney failure
x: The India Hypertension Control Initiative targets hypertension-related deaths from heart attack, stroke and kidney failure.

s: What was NP-NCD earlier known as?
x: NP-NCD was earlier NPCDCS; it uses population-based screening to find high-risk people and link them to care.

s: What is the main approach of NP-NCD?
o: Population-based screening to find high-risk people
x: NP-NCD uses population-based screening to identify high-risk people and link them to care.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the expanded NP-NCD in Andhra Pradesh?
o: It covers mental health and elderly care
It provides free leprosy MDT in place of NLEP
It covers Iodine Deficiency Disorders and tobacco control
It covers fluorosis and oral health
x: AP's expanded NP-NCD covers mental health, elderly care, IDD, tobacco control, fluorosis and oral health. Free leprosy MDT is given under NLEP, not NP-NCD.

s: What does Sustainable Development Goal 3.3 seek to achieve by 2030?
o: Reduce premature NCD deaths by one-third only
Eliminate all forms of environmental pollution
Provide universal mental-health counselling through telemedicine
End epidemics of AIDS, tuberculosis, malaria and neglected tropical diseases
x: SDG 3.3 specifically seeks to end the epidemics of AIDS, tuberculosis, malaria and neglected tropical diseases by 2030.

s: What is the Sustainable Development Goal 3.4 target for premature deaths from non-communicable diseases by 2030?
x: SDG 3.4 calls for reducing premature mortality from non-communicable diseases by one-third through prevention and treatment by 2030.

s:
Consider the following statements about nutrition-related programmes:
1. The National Goitre Control Programme was launched in 1962.
2. Vitamin A prophylaxis against nutritional blindness began in 1992.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Goitre programme began in 1962. Vitamin A prophylaxis began in 1970; 1992 is when the Goitre programme was renamed NIDDCP.

s: In which year was the National Goitre Control Programme renamed the National Iodine Deficiency Disorders Control Programme?
x: It was renamed NIDDCP in 1992.

s: In which year did the Vitamin A prophylaxis programme against nutritional blindness begin?
x: Vitamin A prophylaxis against nutritional blindness began in 1970.

s: Which of the following is NOT a nutrition-related programme?
x: IDD and Vitamin A programmes are nutrition programmes; NLEP is a disease (leprosy) programme.

s: Which of the following correctly gives Andhra Pradesh's 2026 HIV target and its reported three-part status?
x: Andhra Pradesh reported 88%, 87% and 96.2% across the three indicators, with a target for December 2026.

s: What is the target month for Andhra Pradesh's HIV goals?
x: AP's HIV cascade stood at 88%/87%/96.2% in August 2026, with the target set for December 2026.
